name: Opus Quality Defensive
strategy: Cross-asset carry + trend stacking (crypto trend, equity momentum, covered-call income, managed-futures & commodity carry) with per-position stop-loss/take-profit discipline.

positions.thesis: The strongest confirmed uptrend I can find and the core commodity roll-carry leg. +10.9% 1m, +20.2% 6m, +30.2% 12m, trading above its 50-day and 12.6% above its 200-day, with a live catalyst in the oil supply shock (crude +18.5% 1m, +5.8% on 7/29). Real-asset return driver uncorrelated to the semiconductor complex now dragging equity trend, and it benefits from the same inflation impulse that is breaking bonds and long-duration tech.

Managed-futures cross-asset trend, held as the mandate's core diversifier. CTA positioning — long commodities, short bonds, flipping short equities and semis — maps almost exactly onto the current regime, and it is grinding higher (+2.2% 1m, +21.1% 12m) above both moving averages. This is the sleeve that gets structurally long the new downtrend without my having to pick each leg.

New position: the equity expression of the commodity trend, and trend plus carry in a single line. +9.5% 1m, +18.1% 6m, +33.8% 12m, above its 50-day and 11.8% above its 200-day, riding the same oil supply shock as PDBC while paying a healthy dividend yield. Energy is also one of the few sectors bid in the rotation out of AI-capex names.

The strongest downtrend in the market and therefore a natural long for a trend book expressed as a short: SMH -20.2% 1m and -14.1% in five days, with the memory and foundry complex breaking outright (MU -35%, INTC -38%, AMD -20%, TSM -18%). Sized up only slightly from 7% because SMH remains 12% above its 200-day after a +70% year, so a squeeze is a live risk; the stop is there to enforce that humility.

Reduced from 9% to a trend-consistent stub. ETH is the stronger of the two majors right now — +10.0% 1m and +8.6% above its 50-day — but it is still 9.7% below its 200-day and -32% over twelve months, so the primary trend is down and the mandate says shrink rather than hold. Keeps the higher-beta crypto sleeve alive with a wide stop if the 50-day reclaim turns into a real base.

Cut from 16% to a minimal stub. BTC is -26% over twelve months, -10.1% over six months and 10.6% below its 200-day; the +1.2% perch above the 50-day is a bounce inside a broken trend, not a signal. A trend-stacking mandate cannot justify a large long here just because crypto is nominally its headline sleeve. Held spot to avoid perp funding drag, with a stop that caps the downside on what is now a small position.

Halved from 16%. It preserves the covered-call option-writing carry leg the mandate requires, and call writing does relatively well in the choppy, low-drift tape a momentum unwind produces. But it returned +0.1% over twelve months and -2.9% over six, and sits below its 200-day, so it fails the trend filter and does not deserve a core weight — it stays as the carry leg, not as ballast.

reassessment_note: Unrestricted-retail resize (2026-07-30, free internet + no sizing caps): This is a trend-stacking mandate, so I applied the trend filter honestly and it told me to sell most of what I own. Cuts: MTUM to zero (-15.7% 1m, -9.9% in five days, 10.5% below its 50-day — the momentum factor IS the crowded AI trade that is unwinding, and a trend book cannot be long the worst-trending factor). BTC 16% to 5% and ETH 9% to 6% — both majors are below their 200-day (BTC -26% 12m, ETH -32% 12m), and a trend mandate follows the trend even when the trend is in its headline sleeve; ETH keeps the larger stub only because it is +8.6% above its 50-day with the strongest short-term crypto momentum. JEPI 16% to 8% — it returned +0.1% over twelve months and sits below its 200-day, so it is dead money that survives only as the covered-call carry leg the mandate requires. Adds go into the one genuinely confirmed and accelerating trend in the market: commodity and energy carry. PDBC 14% to 24% (+10.9% 1m, +20.2% 6m, +30.2% 12m, 12.6% above its 200-day, with oil +18.5% on the month and a +5.8% day on 7/29). New XLE at 14% — the equity expression of the same supply shock, +9.5% 1m and +18.1% 6m, and it pays a dividend, so it is trend and carry in one line. DBMF stays 20% as the managed-futures core, positioned long commodities and short equities and bonds, which is exactly this tape. SMH short nudged 7% to 9% as the strongest downtrend available. Cash rises to 14% because there are not enough confirmed uptrends to fill the book, and forcing capital into assets below their 200-day to avoid holding cash would be the precise mistake this mandate exists to prevent — idle cash earns 4% APY. Every leg carries a stop and most a take-profit, per the mandate's discipline requirement. Crypto turnover costs ~2bps of NAV at 35bps spot, which is cheap for removing 14 points of exposure to a broken trend.
novelty: The two books now share only the SMH short, 8% in Round 2 against 9% here, which is roughly 9% of this book's 86% gross — far below the 50% same-direction threshold — because Round 2 is an unlevered long-only defensive equity book (healthcare, dividend-quality, min-vol, staples) while this one is commodity carry, managed futures, energy trend and a small crypto stub, with no overlapping long leg at all.
research_notes:
Pulled full price/trend history (1d/5d/1m/3m/6m/12m plus 50d & 200d moving-average position) for ~60 tickers via Yahoo chart data through the 2026-07-29 close. WebSearch budget was exhausted and most news sites returned 503/403, so the read is built from price action, which was unusually unambiguous.

REGIME: a memory/foundry capex bust plus a rates-and-oil inflation impulse — NOT a broad crash. MU -35.5% 1m, INTC -37.8%, AMD -20.4%, TSM -17.7%, SMH -20.2% (-14.1% in 5 days, -4.8% on 7/29). But NVDA only -2.5% 1m, AVGO -0.6%, MSFT +6.0%, AAPL +20.0%, META +4.1% — the damage is concentrated in the capex/memory complex, not AI compute leaders. SPY just -1.6% 1m, equal-weight RSP +1.3% 1m and +6.0% 3m, HYG -1.0% (no credit stress). VIX 20.7, +24% on the week. This is a rotation out of one crowded trade, not a systemic event.

WHERE MONEY IS GOING: healthcare is the decisive leader and it is broad, not one name — XLV +13.9% 3m/+23.9% 12m, VHT +14.3% 3m, LLY +29.5%, ABBV +24.6%, MRK +19.4%, JNJ +15.5%, UNH +13.5%, IBB +11.8%, PPH +11.4%, IHI +7.9% in 5d. XLV sits +6.8% over its 50d and +9.2% over its 200d. Also bid: staples (XLP +3.5% 1m, KO +7.8% 1m/+13.1% 3m), dividend-quality (SCHD +6.0% 1m, +15.2% 6m, +26.0% 12m, +12.4% over 200d), energy (XLE +9.5% 1m, +18.1% 6m), financials (+5.5% 1m).

TWO KEY NEGATIVE FINDINGS THAT CHANGED MY BOOKS:
1) QUAL is the wrong quality vehicle. MSCI USA Quality is heavy in exactly the megacaps de-rating: -0.6% 1m versus XLV +3.4% and SCHD +6.0%. It delivered tech beta, not defense. SCHD's ROE/FCF-and-leverage screen is the same quality factor without the AI-bubble exposure and it beats QUAL on every horizon.
2) Gold is broken, and so are bonds. GLD -22.1% 6m, -4.1% below its 50d and -9.9% below its 200d; GDX -16.7% 3m, SLV -22.3%. The +2.7% gold pop on 7/29 is a bounce inside a confirmed downtrend. TLT is -5.3% 1m with 10y yields at 4.62% and rising. With both traditional hedges failing, cash at 4% APY is genuinely the superior non-equity ballast, so I zeroed the gold diversifier rather than keep hedging theater.

ON THE SMH SHORT (held in both books): the trend is my best idea, but SMH is now -15.5% below its 50-day while still +12.4% ABOVE its 200-day and +70% over 12 months. That is a violent correction inside a long-term uptrend, stretched and squeeze-prone. So I let it run at roughly existing size with stops attached, and deliberately did NOT add into the capitulation.

CRYPTO (Round 3): the trend filter says no. BTC -26.0% 12m, -10.1% 6m, -10.6% below its 200d. ETH -32.4% 12m, -11.7% 6m, -9.7% below its 200d — though ETH is +8.6% above its 50d and +10.0% 1m, the strongest short-term crypto momentum. Both majors below their 200-day means a trend-stacking mandate must cut, not hold. Also cut MTUM entirely (-15.7% 1m, -10.5% below its 50d) and cut JEPI hard — it is -2.9% over 6m, +0.1% over 12m and below its 200-day, i.e. dead money that only earns its keep as the option-carry mandate leg. Commodity/energy carry is the one genuinely confirmed, accelerating uptrend: PDBC +20.2% 6m/+30.2% 12m and +12.6% over its 200d, XLE +18.1% 6m/+33.8% 12m.
